items.title: M-estimators
items.statement: For IID data with law P and an integrable jointly measurable criterion mθ, an M-estimator is a data-measurable exact or oP(1)-approximate maximizer or minimizer of Pn mθ. The maximizing and minimizing forms convert by replacing mθ with −mθ; existence is not asserted.

references.title: Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Stat 210B Lecture 15
Aad W. van der Vaart, Semiparametric Statistics, Lecture 5 §5.3

items.title: Z-estimators
items.statement: For IID data with law P and integrable finite-dimensional estimating functions ψθ, a Z-estimator is a measurable exact or oP(1)-approximate root of Ψn(θ)=Pnψθ. No score equation is inferred from a nonsmooth M-criterion.

references.title: Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Stat 210B Lecture 15
Aad W. van der Vaart, Semiparametric Statistics, Lecture 5 §5.3

items.title: Consistency of M-estimators under a uniform law
items.statement: Uniform convergence in probability of the empirical criterion, positive population separation outside every metric neighborhood of θ0, and an oP(1)-approximate empirical maximizer relative to θ0 imply consistency in probability. The minimizing result follows by sign reversal.

references.title: Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Stat 210B Lecture 15
Aad W. van der Vaart, Semiparametric Statistics, Lecture 5 §5.3
Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 581, Chapter 3 M-estimation

items.title: Consistency of Z-estimators under a uniform law
items.statement: Uniform convergence in probability of a finite-dimensional empirical estimating equation, a separated unique population root, and an oP(1) empirical root residual imply consistency in probability.

references.title: Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Stat 210B Lecture 15
Aad W. van der Vaart, Semiparametric Statistics, Lecture 5 §5.3
Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 581, Chapter 3 M-estimation

items.title: The sample mean as a quadratic M-estimator
items.statement: The negative squared-error sample criterion is uniquely maximized at the sample mean; under a finite second moment its population criterion is uniquely maximized at the mean.

references.title: Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Stat 210B Lecture 15
Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 581, Chapter 3 M-estimation

items.title: Sample medians as absolute-criterion M-estimators
items.statement: The negative absolute-error empirical criterion is uniquely maximized at the middle order statistic for odd n and exactly on the interval between the two middle order statistics for even n; an explicit middle-point selection is measurable.

references.title: Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Stat 210B Lecture 15
Aad W. van der Vaart, Semiparametric Statistics, Lecture 5 §5.3
Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 581, Chapter 3 M-estimation

items.title: A finite-class M-estimator and its uniform law
items.statement: For a Bernoulli criterion indexed by {0,1} with p>0, an exact empirical maximizer is consistent for the unique population maximizer; a direct fourth-moment and summability proof gives the Bernoulli strong law and the finite-class uniform law.

references.title: Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Stat 210B Lecture 15

items.title: An exact M-estimator can fail without population separation
items.statement: With a constant criterion on Θ={0,1}, the alternating exact empirical maximizer has zero uniform criterion error but is not consistent for the fixed population maximizer 0.

references.title: Peter Bartlett, Theoretical Statistics, Stat 210B Lecture 15
